original_test_intent: Verify every required motherboard jumper shunt is present, fully seated and bridges the exact pins/state required by the approved system recipe, without changing configuration during this inspection.
original_method: Bind SUT to motherboard/PCB and recipe revisions; obtain a complete per-designator expected pin-bridge/default/exception table; use powered-down ESD-safe access; qualified operator captures oriented close-ups that show header numbering, shunt seating and actual bridged pins for every entry; compare actual to expected and record missing, loose, extra or mis-set shunts; do not correct within this review step.
manual_activity: Qualified operator photographs actual pin bridges/seating without moving them; agent may reconcile the indexed image set with the approved recipe.
required_inputs: SUT/MB assembly and PCB revision plus product recipe revision
Complete in-scope jumper designator and expected pins/state/default/exception table
Header pin numbering/orientation references and seating criteria
Safe powered-down chassis/ESD inspection and evidence procedure
safety_requirements: De-energize/discharge and use ESD controls before inspection
Verify pin-1/orientation and board revision before judging positions
Do not remove, move or reseat shunts under an inspection-only authorization
Stop on ambiguous numbering, loose/damaged hardware or unsafe access
agent_execution_scope: Compare each indexed close-up to the expected pin bridge/state
Do not open chassis, infer pins from guesswork, move hardware or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve exact recipe and per-jumper setting matrix
Review every discrepancy and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No remote command proves physical shunt seating/pin bridge; visual evidence must be tied to exact header numbering.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a per-designator recipe checklist with oriented close-ups showing bridged pins and seating depth.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All jumpers following the system spec remain the required scope.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Reconcile every shunt against a revision-specific pin-bridge matrix without altering observed state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exhaustive scope, pin orientation, seating and exception handling.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Correct header location alone does not prove a shunt bridges the required pins; this is distinct from row 2284.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Silkscreen pin numbering may be obscured and some recipes vary by SKU; unapproved movement can change boot/security behavior.

project_override_considerations: Any correction/reseat must be a separately authorized action with its own recovery impact; preserve the as-found evidence first.
expected_evidence: Oriented indexed close-ups of every actual shunt and seating

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently request jumper settings to match the system specification.

blocked_analysis.analysis: This is valid manual inspection when the exact recipe matrix and safe access are supplied.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2285 Wistron-HW-00163-V003: approve SUT/motherboard assembly and PCB revision, product recipe revision and complete per-jumper reference-designator, expected bridged pins/state/default plus SKU exception matrix; define pin-1/orientation and seating acceptance, safe powered-down ESD inspection and required photo evidence; confirm as-found inspection only, with any correction/reseat separately authorized.

review_improvement: Preserves the setting/seating scope distinct from location and prevents inspection from silently becoming a configuration change.
independent_technical_reasoning: A jumper setting is defined by which numbered pins are bridged, not by the header's physical location. Similar boards may reverse orientation or vary settings by SKU, and a loose shunt can appear correct from an overview. Each reference therefore needs an oriented close-up and recipe-specific expected state. Changing an observed mismatch would destroy as-found evidence and may alter boot/security behavior, so correction must remain outside this inspection authorization.
